answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 8 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. The island multiplier is published, charged in wander, and whisper lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2636 identities would post 2842 proofs and burn roughly 47 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
